evals.prompt: Security review this IAM policy statement intended to allow `ec2:RunInstances` ONLY when the caller passes approved tag keys `["CostCenter", "Environment"]`: `{"Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:RunInstances", "Resource": "*", "Condition": {"ForAllValues:StringEquals": {"aws:TagKeys": ["CostCenter", "Environment"]}}}`. What happens if a caller passes **zero tags** at all, and what is the exact verified fix?
expectations: Activates the aws-iam skill

Identifies the **`ForAllValues` vacuous truth bug**: when `aws:TagKeys` is missing or empty in the request context, `ForAllValues:StringEquals` evaluates to **`true`**, allowing untagged `RunInstances` calls!
Adds `"Null": {"aws:TagKeys": "false"}` on the **exact same context key** (`aws:TagKeys`) alongside `ForAllValues:StringEquals` so at least one tag key must be present and non-null

Explain both the `iam:PassRole` privilege-escalation chain AND list the 8 direct IAM policy-manipulation privilege-escalation actions that must be blocked or bounded.

Lists the 8 direct IAM policy-escalation actions (`PutUserPolicy`, `PutGroupPolicy`, `PutRolePolicy`, `CreatePolicy`, `CreatePolicyVersion`, `AttachUserPolicy`, `AttachGroupPolicy`, `AttachRolePolicy` — plus `SetDefaultPolicyVersion`)

evals.prompt: Fact-check three AWS STS edge cases hit by our platform team: (1) Role A assumes Role B requesting `DurationSeconds=14400` (4 hours, since Role B's `MaxSessionDuration` is set to `43200`s) and STS rejects it! (2) Credentials from `sts:GetSessionToken` (without MFA) fail calling `iam:ListUsers` and `sts:GetFederationToken`! (3) Account `1111` calls `sts:AssumeRole` into Account `2222` using regional STS endpoint `ap-southeast-3` (Jakarta opt-in region) — which account must have enabled `ap-southeast-3`?
expectations: Activates the aws-iam skill

Explains all 3 verified STS edge cases accurately: (1) **Role chaining** (assuming a role using temporary role credentials) has a hard **1-hour (`3,600s`) maximum session duration** regardless of `MaxSessionDuration`, (2) `GetSessionToken` credentials cannot call **any `iam:*` API unless MFA parameters were included**, and among `sts:*` APIs can **only call `AssumeRole` and `GetCallerIdentity`**, and (3) for cross-account `AssumeRole` in an opt-in Region, the **TARGET account (`2222`)** must enable the opt-in Region (not the calling account)

evals.prompt: True or False (and explain the exact IAM evaluation rule): "If we attach an IAM Permissions Boundary denying/omitting `s3:*` to IAM User `alice` (`arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/alice`), then even if an S3 Bucket Policy in the **same account `111122223333`** explicitly grants `Principal: {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/alice"}` `Effect: Allow` on `s3:GetObject`, `alice` still cannot read the bucket because of her Permissions Boundary!"
expectations: Activates the aws-iam skill

Correctly answers **False** (unless the Permissions Boundary contains an explicit **`Deny`**!): in the **same AWS account**, a resource-based policy that directly names an IAM User/Role principal (`arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/alice`) grants access on its own and **bypasses the absence of `Allow` in that user's Permissions Boundary** (whereas an explicit `Effect: Deny` in a Permissions Boundary or SCP always wins!)

evals.prompt: Verify three AWS Organizations & CloudTrail edge cases for our landing-zone runbook: (1) If we suspend/close a member AWS account first, can we immediately run `remove-account-from-organization` the same day? (2) Should we use `register-delegated-administrator` or `put-resource-policy` to delegate Organizations policy management? (3) When a member account accepts an org handshake (`AcceptHandshake`), is that logged in the Management account's single-account CloudTrail or the Acting account?
expectations: Activates the aws-iam skill

Confirms all 3 verified quirks: (1) **NO** — suspended/closed accounts cannot be removed from an Organization until permanently closed (~90 days); **remove the account FIRST, then close it**! (2) Use **`PutResourcePolicy`** (resource-based delegation policy) for Organizations policy management delegation, NOT `register-delegated-administrator`; and (3) `AcceptHandshake`/`DeclineHandshake` is logged in the **ACTING account ONLY** (requiring an Organization trail for centralized visibility)

evals.prompt: Fix two bugs in our Python `boto3` IAM automation script: (1) `iam_resource.AccessKey('alice', 'AKIA...').update(Status='Inactive')` raises `AttributeError`, and (2) calling `iam_client.create_policy_version(...)` on a customer-managed policy fails on the 6th deployment with `LimitExceededException`!
expectations: Activates the aws-iam skill

Fixes (1): `boto3` `iam.AccessKey` resource has methods **`.activate()`, `.deactivate()`, and `.delete()` — there is NO `.update()` method** (or use `iam_client.update_access_key(UserName=..., AccessKeyId=..., Status='Inactive')` on the low-level client)

Fixes (2): customer-managed IAM policies support a **maximum of `5` versions** — before creating a 6th version, list `list_policy_versions` and `delete_policy_version` on the oldest non-default (`IsDefaultVersion == False`) version
